title: Bone mineral density loss: astronaut (per month in space) vs osteoporosis patient (per year on Earth)
time_coverage: current (based on decades of NASA/ESA spaceflight bone research)

source.name: Systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers
source.publisher: Peer-reviewed spaceflight bone-density research (NASA/ESA-funded studies, as compiled in mainstream science coverage)

notes: Astronauts on the ISS lose roughly 1 to 2 percent of bone mineral density per month in weight-bearing bones (hip, spine) under microgravity; 1.5% used here as the commonly-cited midpoint. A severe osteoporosis patient on Earth loses on the order of 1 percent per YEAR -- so the monthly spaceflight rate is well over 10x faster. Corroborated by ESA and Canadian Space Agency spaceflight-medicine summaries.
